ritualsnotrolls.guide.title: Rituals Not Rolls
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.0.title: Getting started
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.0.body:
Find Knowledge Pages in loot, including mob drops, trial spawners and vaults. Configured enchanted-book drops become their associated pages. Each page teaches one material for one enchantment. Craft a page with three leather to make a Knowledge Book, or throw them onto the table to bind and shelve the first book for that enchantment.

Put your pages or books in chiseled bookshelves within %s blocks of the table. Place matching materials on nearby Ritual Pedestals.

Throw one tool, weapon, piece of armor, or book toward the table. It catches the item and applies the highest levels the arrangement can afford. You do not need to open this screen to start.

Ordinary, unmarked materials stay on their pedestals. Start with those before trying catalysts.
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.1.title: Your library
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.1.body:
Knowledge comes from the nearby shelves, not from books or binders in your inventory. A book can collect different material discoveries for the same enchantment.

Use a Knowledge Book to read it. Auto-Add collects newly acquired matching pages; moving pages around your inventory does not absorb them. Gather pages pulls new matching discoveries from your inventory, including expanded storage. You can also tear discoveries back out.

Several shelves can contribute knowledge. A missing or changed datapack entry stays in the book as inactive knowledge until that entry returns.

The table lists the enchantments your library knows. Search by enchantment name or a known material. Right-click the search box to clear it. Hold an item when opening the table to show enchantments it accepts, plus any already on it. Empty hands and completely non-enchantable items show everything. Hover an enchantment to read its description.

Shift-click an enchantment in the table list to summon its Knowledge Book from a shelf. The book flies above the table and drops. If only loose pages are available, each click retrieves one page.

Throw pages onto the table to file them into nearby books. Many pages can fly at once, even to the same book. A page stays loose if any library book already knows that discovery.

If no book of an enchantment exists, throw leather onto the table too. Three leather gather around one page, form a book, and send it into an empty chiseled bookshelf slot. Leather can come from several stacks, but must be thrown by the same player as the page. Surplus leather and duplicate pages stay loose. Different enchantments can bind at once; more discoveries for the same enchantment wait for its new book. Existing books never cost leather.

Throw a complete Knowledge Book onto the table to send it into a random open chiseled bookshelf slot. With no destination, it stays put.

Craft a Knowledge Binder with four leather, four paper and one string: leather in the four corners, string in the center and paper in the remaining slots. It holds %s pages on this server, counting duplicate copies. Reducing its configured limit preserves pages already inside.

A new binder has Auto-collect and Skip duplicates on. Every second it collects loose pages from your inventory, including expanded storage. The filter keeps one page for each enchantment and material discovery in that binder, without checking your library. Turn Skip duplicates off to collect extra copies. Turn Auto-collect off to keep pages loose.

Double-click a binder in an inventory to gather pages from the open container and your inventory, including expanded storage. This works with Auto-collect off, but still respects Skip duplicates and the capacity limit. Right-click the binder to browse twelve cards across two leaves. Use the arrows or mouse wheel to turn pages. Click a card to take one page, or Shift-click to take up to 64. Collection pauses while this screen is open.

Throw the binder onto the table to file its contents. This server checks up to %s pages every 20 ticks, then lets their transfers run together. Throw leather alongside it to bind missing books at three leather each. Duplicates and pages that cannot be filed stay inside. The binder drops back down after processing and its library transfers finish.

An enchanted book can also be crafted alone into one random page for a configured enchantment. Other enchantments stay on the returned book. Use JEI, EMI or REI's Uses key on a page or enchanted book to see these recipes; knowledge variants stay out of the item list.
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.2.title: Reading power
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.2.body:
A material has a different affinity for each enchantment. Weakest, Weak, Average, Strong and Strongest compare it with the strongest material for that same enchantment. These labels are not enchantment levels.

Base describes the material itself. Effective describes its current contribution from placed pedestals, including catalysts and routes. Effective is hidden when that contribution is zero.

Potential is the available power for one enchantment. The actual result also depends on the target item, sharing and conflicts.

Adding distinct materials helps. A second unmarked copy of the same item adds no power. Only the strongest known affinity matching an item counts; learning overlapping item and group entries does not stack them.
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.3.title: Consumed offerings
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.3.body:
Attach a Consumption Catalyst to a pedestal to spend its displayed material for extra power. Each participating marked pedestal spends one item. The catalyst stays.

This server uses a %s-times consumption multiplier. Consumed copies of the same item then keep %s, %s, %s and %s of that multiplied power for the first four copies.

The strongest copy counts first. Copies count together across shelves for the same enchantment. Applying and subtracting count separately. An unmarked copy does not advance this count.

An offering breaks into item particles when the trail reaches it. If the ritual is interrupted, reserved offerings are returned. Repeated materials help, but with the default curve each extra copy adds less.
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.4.title: Enchantability
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.4.body:
Enchantability is an item property. With this setting enabled, low ratings need more ritual power and high ratings need less. It changes the cost, not your material discoveries.

On this server the baseline is %s. Ratings above it pass through a configurable curve; the default gives progressively smaller gains. A rating of %s would cost %s of the baseline requirement. Item enchantability is currently %s.

Books are neutral. Existing enchantments remain unless you can improve them or remove whole levels with subtraction.

The bundled multi-level vanilla enchantments can reach level X. Higher levels need increasingly more power. Enchantments that normally have only one level still stop at I. Datapacks can change these limits.
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.5.title: Chains & conflicts
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.5.body:
Books connect to useful pedestals in nearby branches. A return route can revisit a pedestal and add power without taking another item. Chaining is currently %s; a return visit adds %s of that pedestal's contribution.

When several enchantments use one pedestal, they share its contribution if each can still change a level. If there is not enough for both, the stronger available enchantment is tried first. Equal power uses a stable enchantment-ID order.

Enchantments in a conflict group cost more together. The default doubles the requirement for each additional member. Existing enchantments count first. This is a cost penalty, so conflicting enchantments can coexist when enough power is available.

Rearranging shelves and pedestals can change routes, sharing and the final result.
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.6.title: Experience
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.6.body:
Place an Experience Catalyst in a pedestal's displayed item slot. It uses XP from the player who threw the target. It does not consume itself.

Each catalyst allows up to %s equivalent levels of XP for a %s power bonus. One fully funded catalyst costs %s XP; two together cost %s XP.

These are the points needed to earn those levels from zero, not levels subtracted from your current level number. The combined cost rises as you add catalysts.

If you have less XP, the ritual uses what you can afford and gives a smaller bonus. With no XP, it can still use material power alone. Payment happens once on success. XP gained after capture stays with you. The table footer shows the current payable amount.
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.7.title: Removing & failures
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.7.body:
Attach a Subtraction Catalyst to reverse a material's contribution. Enough negative power lowers existing enchantments, including curses. Reaching zero removes the enchantment.

Only whole levels are removed. Weak subtraction stores no partial progress and spends nothing when it cannot change a level. Positive and negative contributions cancel before the result is chosen. Consumption can strengthen subtraction by spending its offering.

A failed chain scatters; it does not spend its offerings. Other successful chains may still finish. Interrupting a ritual returns any reserved offerings.

If nothing happens, check that the target is one item, the shelves contain the right knowledge, and the pedestals can supply enough power to change a level. Keep the table, shelves and participating pedestals intact until completion.
enchantment.minecraft.aqua_affinity.desc: Removes the mining-speed penalty from being underwater.
enchantment.minecraft.bane_of_arthropods: Deals extra damage to arthropods and briefly slows them.
enchantment.minecraft.binding_curse.desc: Keeps equipped gear locked on until it breaks or the wearer dies.
enchantment.minecraft.blast_protection.d: Reduces explosion damage and explosion knockback.
enchantment.minecraft.breach.desc: Reduces how much the target's armor protects against mace attacks.
enchantment.minecraft.channeling.desc: Strikes trident targets with lightning during thunderstorms when exposed to the sky.
enchantment.minecraft.density.desc: Adds mace smash-attack damage for each block fallen.
enchantment.minecraft.depth_strider.desc: Reduces the movement penalty from walking underwater.
enchantment.minecraft.efficiency.desc: Increases mining speed when using an appropriate tool.
enchantment.minecraft.fire_aspect.desc: Sets targets on fire when struck.
enchantment.minecraft.fire_protection.de: Reduces fire damage and the time spent burning.
enchantment.minecraft.fortune.desc: Increases the drops from certain mined blocks.
enchantment.minecraft.frost_walker.desc: Freezes water underfoot and protects against magma-block damage.
enchantment.minecraft.impaling.desc: Deals extra trident damage to aquatic mobs.
enchantment.minecraft.infinity.desc: Fires ordinary arrows without consuming them; one arrow is still required.
enchantment.minecraft.looting.desc: Increases eligible mob drops and the chance of rare drops.
enchantment.minecraft.loyalty.desc: Returns a thrown trident to its owner.
enchantment.minecraft.luck_of_the_sea.de: Improves the chance of treasure when fishing and reduces junk catches.
enchantment.minecraft.lure.desc: Shortens the wait for a fishing bite.
enchantment.minecraft.mending.desc: Uses collected experience orbs to repair the enchanted item.
enchantment.minecraft.multishot.desc: Fires additional crossbow projectiles while using ammunition for one shot.
enchantment.minecraft.piercing.desc: Allows crossbow arrows to pass through multiple entities and shields.
enchantment.minecraft.quick_charge.desc: Reduces the time needed to load a crossbow.
enchantment.minecraft.respiration.desc: Extends the time the wearer can breathe underwater.
enchantment.minecraft.riptide.desc: Propels the user with a trident while in water or rain.
enchantment.minecraft.silk_touch.desc: Makes eligible blocks drop themselves instead of their usual drops.
enchantment.minecraft.smite.desc: Deals extra damage to undead mobs.
enchantment.minecraft.soul_speed.desc: Moves faster on soul sand and soul soil, sometimes costing boot durability.
enchantment.minecraft.sweeping_edge.desc: Increases damage dealt by a sword's sweeping attack.
enchantment.minecraft.thorns.desc: Can hurt attackers, using extra armor durability.
enchantment.minecraft.unbreaking.desc: Gives the item a chance to avoid losing durability when used.
enchantment.minecraft.vanishing_curse.de: Makes the item disappear on death.
enchantment.minecraft.wind_burst.desc: Launches the user upward after a successful mace smash attack.

ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.0.caption: Books teach enchantments. Materials on pedestals supply power. Throw your target onto the table.
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.1.caption: Pages fly into library books. Add leather to bind missing books, or throw a binder to file its contents.
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.2.caption: Different materials supply different power. Each pedestal contributes its displayed item.
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.3.caption: The attached Consumption Catalyst spends its offering. Item fragments mark the moment it is taken.
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.4.caption: High enchantability lowers power costs with diminishing gains. Books have neutral costs.
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.5.caption: Magical trails follow useful pedestals and gather around the target. Shelf placement affects routes.
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.6.caption: The displayed Experience Catalyst draws XP from the player for a power bonus. The catalyst remains.
ritualsnotrolls.guide.chapter.7.caption: Subtraction Catalysts reverse material power to remove whole enchantment levels, including curses.
